title: What's the weather like?
goal: Talk about the weather and the seasons with verbs that have no subject at all — and get ready for a real Georgian winter.
bekal: ask about and describe today's weather
use verbs with no subject: წვიმს, თოვს, ცხელა
name the four seasons and what they're like
use the weather as a conversation opener

dialogs.title: დიალოგი — November in Tbilisi
dialogs.intro: Ani calls Nino before leaving the house. It's her first real winter. Notice the weather verbs — not one of them has a subject, and none of them needs a pronoun.

lines.speaker: ანი:
lines.id: Hi, Nino! What's the weather like outside?

lines.speaker: ნინო:
lines.id: Cold and rainy. Take an umbrella!

lines.speaker: ანი:
lines.id: Raining again? It rained yesterday too.

lines.speaker: ნინო:
lines.id: It's November, Ani. This is normal.

lines.speaker: ნინო:
lines.id: Eight degrees. In winter it gets even colder.
lines.literal: eight — degree. winter-in — still — more — cold-is.

lines.speaker: ნინო:
lines.id: Rarely in Tbilisi. But in the mountains there's a lot of snow.
lines.literal: Tbilisi-in — rarely. mountain-in — though — much — snow-is.

lines.speaker: ნინო:
lines.id: Really? Then this winter we're going to Gudauri!

lines.speaker: ანი:
lines.id: Sure, but first I need a warm jacket.
lines.literal: good, but — first — warm — jacket — I-need.

lines.speaker: ნინო:
lines.id: We'll buy one together tomorrow. Today, don't forget your umbrella!
lines.literal: tomorrow — together — let's-buy. today — umbrella — not — forgotten-to-you!

notes: **Weather verbs have no subject at all.** წვიმს (it's raining), თოვს (it's snowing), ცხელა (it's hot), ცივა (it's cold), ქარია (it's windy). Unlike English (*it rains*) or German, there is no "it" to write — the verb alone is a complete sentence.

**ცხელა / ცივა are not the same as ცხელი / ცივი.** The **-ა** forms are complete sentences about a state: *ცივა* = "it's cold (here)". The **-ი** forms are adjectives that need a noun: *ცივი წყალი* (cold water). ⚠️ Don't say *ცივი არის* about the weather — just **ცივა**.

**წვიმდა = "it rained (yesterday)".** This is your first brush with the past tense, and we're deliberately letting it slide by. The pattern: present weather verbs end in **-ს**, past ones in **-და**. წვიმ**ს** → წვიმ**და**, თოვ**ს** → თოვ**და**. Unit 17 opens up the whole system.
**გუშინაც = გუშინ + ც (yesterday too)**, and **კიდეც** = კიდევ + ც (also, what's more). The -ც particle from unit 1 is still hard at work.

**უფრო = more.** This is how you compare at A1: *უფრო ცივა* (colder), *უფრო კარგია* (better), *უფრო დიდი* (bigger). For "than", use the ending **-ზე**: *თბილისი ბათუმზე დიდია* (Tbilisi is bigger than Batumi).
**თოვლი მოდის** — literally "snow comes", another way to say it's snowing. The verb **მოდის** (comes) from unit 9 turns up in an unexpected place.
**ჯერ = first, (not) yet.** *ჯერ არა* (not yet), *ჯერ ვერ ვლაპარაკობ* (I can't speak yet). A small word that rescues a lot of sentences.

grammars.title: Weather: sentences without a subject
after: To ask: **როგორია ამინდი?** (what's the weather like?) or, shorter, **ამინდი როგორია?**. For tomorrow: **ხვალ როგორი ამინდი იქნება?** (khval rogori amindi ikneba).

grammars.title: The four seasons
after: ⚠️ Notice the endings don't match: გაზაფხულ**ზე** and შემოდგომა**ზე** take -ზე, while ზაფხულ**ში** and ზამთარ**ში** take -ში. There's no sensible reason; just memorize these four forms.
Georgia has four truly distinct seasons. Temperatures in Tbilisi range from −5°C (23°F) in January to +35°C (95°F) in August.

blocks.title: Five weather sentences that start a conversation
items: **დღეს ძალიან ცივა.** — It's very cold today.
**ხვალ წვიმა იქნება?** (khval ts'vima ikneba) — Will it rain tomorrow?
**ინდონეზიაში მუდამ ცხელა.** — It's always hot in Indonesia.
**თოვლი პირველად ვნახე.** (tovli p'irvelad vnakhe) — I saw snow for the first time.

blocks.text: That last sentence is worth more than it looks. To Georgians, an adult who has never seen snow is hard to imagine, and saying so almost always opens a long conversation — often ending with an invitation to the mountains. In return, a question you'll hear a lot is *ინდონეზიაში ზამთარი არ არის?* (isn't there a winter in Indonesia?).

⚠️ A practical warning if you come from somewhere warm: a Tbilisi winter isn't just "a bit chilly". January regularly drops below freezing, and old buildings are often cold inside. Three things you can't do without: **თბილი ქურთუკი** (a warm jacket), **ხელთათმანები** (gloves), and shoes that won't slip on **ყინული** (ice). Buying them in Georgia is cheaper and smarter than bringing them from home.

exercises.prompt: Complete with the right weather verb.
Add the right season ending (-ში or -ზე).
Put the words in the right order.

answers: როგორია ამინდი? — წვიმს და ცივა. — რამდენი გრადუსია? — ზამთარში უფრო ცივა. — ქოლგა წაიღე.
დღეს როგორია ამინდი? — ცივა და წვიმს. — რამდენი გრადუსია? — ზამთარში უფრო ცივა. — ინდონეზიაში თოვლი არასდროს არ მოდის. — ქოლგა წაიღე!
